units.sourceHTML: Calling C from Wren
units.originalInnerHTML: Calling C from Wren

units.sourceHTML:
When we are ensconced within the world of Wren, the external C world is
“foreign” to us. There are two reasons we might want to bring some foreign
flavor into our VM:
units.originalInnerHTML:
When we are ensconced within the world of Wren, the external C world is
“foreign” to us. There are two reasons we might want to bring some foreign
flavor into our VM:

units.sourceHTML: We want to execute code written in C.
units.originalInnerHTML: We want to execute code written in C.

units.sourceHTML: We want to store raw C data.
units.originalInnerHTML: We want to store raw C data.

units.sourceHTML: Since Wren is object-oriented, behavior lives in methods, so for the former we have foreign methods. Likewise, data lives in objects, so for the latter, we define foreign classes. This page is about the first, foreign methods. The next page covers foreign classes.
units.originalInnerHTML: Since Wren is object-oriented, behavior lives in methods, so for the former we have foreign methods. Likewise, data lives in objects, so for the latter, we define foreign classes. This page is about the first, foreign methods. The next page covers foreign classes.

units.sourceHTML: A foreign method looks to Wren like a regular method. It is defined on a Wren class, it has a name and signature, and calls to it are dynamically dispatched. The only difference is that the body of the method is written in C.
units.originalInnerHTML: A foreign method looks to Wren like a regular method. It is defined on a Wren class, it has a name and signature, and calls to it are dynamically dispatched. The only difference is that the body of the method is written in C.

The ⟦CODE0⟧ keyword tells Wren that the method ⟦CODE1⟧ is declared on ⟦CODE2⟧,
but implemented in C. Both static and instance methods can be foreign.
units.originalInnerHTML: The foreign keyword tells Wren that the method add() is declared on Math, but implemented in C. Both static and instance methods can be foreign.

units.sourceHTML: Binding Foreign Methods #
units.originalInnerHTML: Binding Foreign Methods #

units.sourceHTML: When you call a foreign method, Wren needs to figure out which C function to execute. This process is called binding. Binding is performed on-demand by the VM. When a class that declares a foreign method is executed – when the ⟦CODE0⟧ statement itself is evaluated – the VM asks the host application for the C function that should be used for the foreign method.
units.originalInnerHTML: When you call a foreign method, Wren needs to figure out which C function to execute. This process is called binding. Binding is performed on-demand by the VM. When a class that declares a foreign method is executed – when the class statement itself is evaluated – the VM asks the host application for the C function that should be used for the foreign method.

units.sourceHTML: It does this through the ⟦CODE0⟧ callback you give it when you first configure the VM. This callback isn’t the foreign method itself. It’s the binding function your app uses to look up foreign methods.
units.originalInnerHTML: It does this through the bindForeignMethodFn callback you give it when you first configure the VM. This callback isn’t the foreign method itself. It’s the binding function your app uses to look up foreign methods.

units.sourceHTML: The important part is that it returns a pointer to a C function to use for that foreign method. Wren does this binding step once when the class definition is first executed. It then keeps the function pointer you return and associates it with that method. This way, calls to the foreign method are fast.

units.sourceHTML: Arguments passed from Wren are not passed as C arguments, and the method’s return value is not a C return value. Instead – you guessed it – we go through the slot array.
units.originalInnerHTML: Arguments passed from Wren are not passed as C arguments, and the method’s return value is not a C return value. Instead – you guessed it – we go through the slot array.

units.sourceHTML:
When a foreign method is called from Wren, the VM sets up the slot array with
the receiver and arguments to the call. As in calling Wren from C, the receiver
object is in slot zero, and arguments are in consecutive slots after that.
units.originalInnerHTML:
When a foreign method is called from Wren, the VM sets up the slot array with
the receiver and arguments to the call. As in calling Wren from C, the receiver
object is in slot zero, and arguments are in consecutive slots after that.

units.sourceHTML: While your foreign method is executing, the VM is completely suspended. No other fibers run until your foreign method returns. You should not try to resume the VM from within a foreign method by calling ⟦CODE0⟧ or ⟦CODE1⟧. The VM is not re-entrant.
units.originalInnerHTML: While your foreign method is executing, the VM is completely suspended. No other fibers run until your foreign method returns. You should not try to resume the VM from within a foreign method by calling wrenCall() or wrenInterpret(). The VM is not re-entrant.
